data.name: ForestTalk
data.shortDescription: Actually talk to Kelvin and Virginia. Kelvin, now deaf, still has plenty to say. Chat through his notepad or hit O for a quick shortcut. Give him real in-game orders. Deep customization included.
data.description:
ForestTalk turns Kelvin and Virginia into real companions, not silent bots you just watch.

💬 How to talk to them
With Kelvin, open his notepad and press T to type. You can also press O while nearby and looking at him, no notepad needed. Virginia works the same way: get close, look at her, and press O, if she's willing.

🧠 Kelvin, your companion
I put a lot of effort into making him aware of his surroundings: nearby danger, your state, the weather, what he's doing. This mod assumes the crash left him deaf, but he can still speak. He's not a bot you click through, he's your companion, and he'll always have something to say. Warm personality, a bit shaken by what he's been through, with a strong moral compass against the forest.

You can also give him real orders through chat: bring logs, repair the camp, build a fire, stay put, follow you, and more. Real orders he carries out in-game.

🌿 Virginia, an independent soul
Virginia can talk with you too, on her own terms: a fully independent person. She can't be given orders or commands, she'll only chat if she feels like it.

⚠️ Real environmental awareness
Both react to what's actually happening: danger, injuries, hunger or thirst, night, rain. I dug deep into the game's code so this isn't a chat bolted on top, they react to what's going on with you.

👀 Bonus: let them see what you see
Type !look plus your message (e.g. !look what do you think of our base?) to send a screenshot along with it. A fun little extra, not required. Heads up: capturing it pauses the game for a split second.

⚙️ Deep customization
Choose between several AI providers: Player2 (a button to generate your API key instantly), OpenAI, Gemini, OpenRouter, or your own custom/local server. Adjust how often they speak on their own, toggle danger comments, write custom personality notes, and more.

Surviving the forest is no longer something you do alone. Kelvin and Virginia become real friends to face the island with.

Sons of the Forest gives you a random appearance every time you join a server, and there is no way to choose. This mod lets you pick the one you want and automatically reapplies it every time your player spawns, so you stay the same character.

Press F9 in game to cycle through the eight appearances. The current one is shown on screen as you cycle. Your choice is saved and applied automatically on every spawn.

If your keyboard has no F keys, or you would rather pick one directly, press F1 to open the console and use the CHARACTER command.

Client side only. Nothing needs to be installed on a dedicated server. Your appearance replicates through normal game networking, so other players see your choice even if they do not have the mod installed.

Source: https://github.com/JustinOros/sotf-character-select

data.name: Freshwater is Drinkable
data.shortDescription: Running water is safe (except when contaminated). Stagnant water is not.
data.description:
REQUIRES https://sotf-mods.com/mods/brutechiefton/uicoordinator


What to expect
--
Filling a flask or pot from a clean source will give you clean water. Drinking from a clean source will not make you sick, it will actually clear some sickness (just like clean/boiled water).

Doing the same at a dirty water source will still give you dirty water and make you sick as normal.

*Note: Only the water sources on the surface have been mapped. 


The mod works by querying against the water graph to find the nearest node. An unmapped water source will therefore use the nearest one, which may or may not not make sense. 


If this bothers you, please use the in-game editor (F7, add last target) to add a node and program it as desired.


Caves and their water sources are currently unmapped.*


Details
--
The mod comes with a water graph that I drew by hand. I marked all the rivers and streams as clean, and every stagnant pool/pond as dirty. 

Each new save's water graph will be loaded from this canonical graph. You can see and edit the water graph by pressing F7. 

Changes made will be saved when you save your game. Different saves can have different graphs.

To overwrite the default water graph, press export. 
To reload the default, press reload.

Dedicated server graphs cannot be edited at this time.

data.name: UICoordinator
data.shortDescription: Enable cursor when any menu is open. Disable when they're all closed.
data.description:
UICoordinator provides reference-counted ownership of menu input. While one or more mod menus hold a lease, UICoordinator unlocks and displays the cursor, places the game input system into menu mode, and suppresses mouse-look. When the final menu releases its lease, the previous cursor and input state are restored.

This prevents independent mod menus from fighting over the cursor or restoring gameplay input while another menu remains open.

Download and check out the readme if you'd like to use it for your own mods.

data.name: Chronos
data.shortDescription: Set day length in real minutes and season length in in-game days, per save, while you play.
data.description:
Day length as a count of real minutes, season length as a count of in-game days, changed at any time in a loaded save. The game gives you four presets, picked at world setup before you know how that world plays, and changing your mind later means editing the save.

**Day length.** The vanilla presets in real time: Short 29.4 minutes, Default 58.7, Long 2h 58m, Realistic 24h. Custom takes anything from 0.1 to 10080 minutes. The panel splits the result into daylight and night. Night runs 2.7 times faster, so a 60-minute day gives you 41 minutes of light.

**Season length.** Presets in in-game days per season: 3, 5, 10, 91. Custom takes 1 to 120 whole days, since a season turns over at midnight. The season is worked out from the current day, so switching the calendar re-reads the year you already played.

**Snow keeps pace.** Snow is a height line that winter walks down the mountains at a fixed rate. On short days a season can end before the line has finished moving. Chronos scales that rate with your day length.

**Usage.** Load a save, open Options, then Mods, then Chronos. Turn on the day override, the season override or both, pick a preset or type your own number, close the panel. Values live inside the save and travel with it.

**Multiplayer.** Works in co-op. Every player needs the mod and the same numbers. The clock comes from the host, but hunger, thirst and the season turn over on each player's own day length. Dedicated servers are untested.

**Compatibility.** Chronos writes the clock speed (TimeOfDayHolder.GetBaseSpeedMultiplier), the season durations (SeasonsManager.GetSeasonDurations) and eight transition fields on SnowHeightManager. Another mod that writes any of them will fight it, and the one that applied last wins.

**Install.** Install RedLoader and run the game once, then unpack the archive into the game folder. You should end up with Mods/Chronos.dll and Mods/Chronos/manifest.json.

Source: github.com/Cyace84/sotf-chronos (MIT)

data.name: Mason Line
data.shortDescription: Build from here to there. Two stakes, a cord between them, and every log you set down snaps to it.
data.description:
A craftable guide line for straight walls. The game stacks logs perfectly, but the angle comes from the first log, dropped by hand with nothing to line up against, and it cannot be nudged afterwards. Mason Line supplies it: plant a stake where the wall starts and another where it ends, a cord pulls tight between them, and anything you set down beside the cord snaps onto it.

Crafted from 2 sticks and 1 rope on the crafting mat.

**Controls.** No custom keybinds. Left-click plants a stake, first A then B. Hold Dismantle (C by default) on a stake to collect the line and get the bundle back.

**What snaps.** Logs flat or standing, standing sticks, campfires, rocks. Anything you set down loose on open ground. Guidebook blueprints, the ghosts you fill in piece by piece, do not.

**Multiple lines.** Each bundle is one line and they all work at once; a log goes to the closest cord. Aim a new line's first stake at a standing one and it lands exactly on it, so a run can turn a corner. Squaring the angle between two lines is still your job.

**Settings.** Snap distance, reach past the stakes and stake magnet, in the mod menu.

**Co-op.** Works in a peer-to-peer game. Lines are private: you see your own stakes, and only your own placements snap to them. The logs themselves are placed by the game as usual, so everyone sees the same wall. Dedicated servers are untested.

**Limitations.** Lines are not part of the save: reload and the line is gone, its bundle back in your pack. The cord is a guide, not an object, so everything walks through it.

**Mod conflicts.** The bundle takes item id 9417. If another mod already owns it, Mason Line refuses to register rather than overwrite, and says so in the log; `UserData/MasonLine.cfg` can point it elsewhere. 
Bug reports: attach `_Redloader/Latest.log`. 
Thanks to ToniMacaroni for RedLoader and SonsSdk.

Full description and source: [GitHub](https://github.com/Cyace84/sotf-mason-line) (MIT)

data.name: Gerald R. Ford-class aircraft carriers
data.shortDescription: Driver your CVN-80 to project power anywhere. You can even build on the deck.
data.description:
This is an aircraft carrier with a full collision volume that allows you to place buildings and blueprints on its deck.
This aircraft carrier is fully controllable; you can steer it to any location on the map.
It also includes a feature that instantly teleports Kevin to your location; you can disable this feature and the driving function in the settings.
You can choose from five preset aircraft carrier spawn locations. You can also save them to any location.

Press the ‘+’ key on the numeric keypad to be teleport to the aircraft carrier's control tower.
Use WASD to move horizontally, Q and E to rotate the aircraft carrier, and Page Up and Page Down to ascend or descend.
Press the ‘+’ key on the numeric keypad a second time to exit drive mode.

Press the “K” key to teleport Kevin 1.5 meters in front of your viewpoint.
I had originally planned to teleport Virginia, but she uses an extremely complex LOD system. Forcing teleport her would cause a lot of problems.
Since someone has already implemented this feature, you can disable it in the settings to ensure compatibility with other mods.

Press the ‘-’ key on the numeric keypad to select one of the five preset locations for the aircraft carrier.
It comes with five user-defined locations. You can drive the aircraft carrier to your preferred location and save those coordinates.
Mod will remember the location of your aircraft carrier, including custom locations.

data.name: Radio Alarm Trap _But is US Military Base Alarm
data.shortDescription: This mod replaces the sound effects for the Radio Alarm Trap with the actual U.S. Military Base Alarm. Fully compatible with your custom radio music
data.description:
This mod dynamically intercepts the original siren events via the Harmony Patch and mutes them.
It also registers a separate FMOD container that contains a modified version of the game’s original sotf_music_radio.bank file. This modified .bank file preserves the developer’s original 3D sound effects and distance attenuation settings, while replacing the siren sound with an authentic U.S. Military Base Alarm.
I have also stored separate dictionaries for each alarm, allowing them to be played or muted independently at the same time, just like in the original game.

The alarm sound is taken from an actual alarm that was played during the DC military lockdown in mid-2021. I processed the audio, boosting it by 5 dB and removing the background noise.

As mentioned earlier, because a separate FMOD container has been registered, this mod is fully compatible with custom radio music, so you don't need to make any changes to the radio music.
You can actually customize the alarm sound to be any other sound (under 43 seconds) by simply modifying the sound file in alarm_custom_V2.bank.

1.0.1 Added settings menu, along with hot-swap functionality and a volume control slider. It is important to note that the 3D effect is created by the game developer in FMOD; increasing the volume only raises the sound level when the player is within the listening range—it does not expand the listening range itself.

- **Universal Decimal Support:** Automatically handles both periods (0.5) and commas (0,5) for number inputs, preventing errors for international players.

data.name: Enable Building in Caves
data.shortDescription: Allows building in caves and removes parts of cave entrances
data.description:
##Building in caves


###Features
- Allows you to build inside caves, cellars and ice caves.
- Opens up cave entrances to carry logs or stones in.
- Allows you to keep logs / stones when entering or leaving bunkers.
- You can even get power inside by placing solar panels outside the cave.


##Configuration:
- **Dont open Caves:** When enabled the game will not open up cave entrances when loading into the world. Does require a restart when changed.


- **Allow actors to traverse caves:** When enabled the game will allow actors to go in and out of caves.


- **Allow GPS to lose signal:** When enabled the GPS will lose signal when entering a cave, when disabled it will still show the outside map.


- **Switch to City filter when entering Cave (Blue Fix):** Will switch the filter to City when entering a cave to remove the blue hue inside caves.


- **Keep Logs or Stones when entering Caves or Bunkers:** When entering a cave or bunker with an animation, any logs or stone in your hands will be returned to you once the animation has finished.


- **Easy Bunkers:** Easy transportation of logs or stones into bunkers, by just throwing them onto the entrance **(disabled by default)**


- **Disable collect Items UI inside Caves:** Will disable the *Collect x of Items* reminder inside caves, will also disable the reminder when blueprints are placed inside caves.


###For even more building in caves fun you should also install: https://sotf-mods.com/mods/tempbito/placestructureanywhere


>Enjoy and have fun!


##Please report any issues you may encounter, thanks!

The mod currently changes the headlights of the golfcarts. Features include:

- Improved look of the headlights and removed the jagged edge to increase realism

- Added high beams, default hotkey H

- Added corner lighting, the lighting angle moves with your steering to light up corners better.

- Headlights can be configured to always be on.

Configuration can be done through the option menu. Headlights always on does not take effect until reboot.

### Corner lighting

Corner lighting is a feature commonly found on modern cars. The headlights move in the steering direction. This mod does the same thing.

The strength of the corner lighting can be adjusted in the settings. 1 means it directly mirrors your steering, where as 0 disables it entirely.

### Info


Multiplayer currently isn't supported (yet). It works on servers, but other players will see the default lighting.

data.name: Realistic meat dryer
data.shortDescription: Meat season... or freezing it
data.description:
Realistic Meat Dryer is a mod designed to improve the survival experience in Sons of the Forest, making the meat drying process much more realistic and in line with the game's environmental conditions. Instead of constant drying independent of the weather, this mod adjusts the drying speed based on the season and ambient temperature, adding an extra level of challenge and immersion for the player.

During spring and summer, when the weather is warm and favorable, meat dries quickly, allowing food to be processed more efficiently and with less risk of spoilage. In contrast, in autumn and winter, the process slows down due to low temperatures and adverse weather conditions. This more accurately reflects how cold and humidity affect natural drying in real life.

An important detail is that the increased drying speed is only activated if the player places a campfire directly under the drying rack. This mechanic is key to achieving good results, especially during winter. Without a nearby heat source, the meat barely dries, simulating a cold environment where natural drying becomes ineffective.

This forces the player to plan better: strategically building campfires, managing timing according to the seasons, and choosing when and where to dry meat. Rather than relying on a simplified system, players must adapt to the surrounding conditions and take advantage of what each season offers to ensure their survival.

data.name: DynamicLighting
data.shortDescription: God said, "Let there be light," and the modders obeyed.
data.description:
This mod for Sons of the Forest is designed to unlock the full visual potential of the game's lighting system. By default, many in-game light sources—especially decorative or atmospheric ones—do not have dynamic shadows enabled, despite having the capability to support them. This oversight can make environments feel flat or unnatural in dark settings, caves, or when interacting with crafted structures. This mod fixes that.

It automatically detects and processes specific light sources in the world, enabling dynamic shadows where they were previously disabled. The mod not only activates shadows, but also fine-tunes various light parameters such as range, intensity, bounce intensity, color temperature, and more. Each light type is adjusted individually depending on its context and structure—for example:

Hanging skull lights and skull fires have their shadows enabled and adjusted for atmospheric warmth.

Wall torches receive a realistic color temperature (1600K) and bounce to simulate flame lighting more naturally.

Spotlights like those on poles or structures are adjusted for proper projection distance, brightness, and shadow culling.

All changes respect the structure’s original style while making lights more visually impactful and immersive.

These tweaks enhance the mood of the game without overexposing or breaking its native art direction. The lighting feels more alive, shadows behave naturally, and night scenes become more believable and engaging.

Whether you're deep in the forest at night, exploring an abandoned cave, or simply walking by crafted structures, you'll notice more realism, atmosphere, and depth thanks to this mod’s subtle but important improvements.

data.name: Effigies
data.shortDescription: We don't need sanity. Intimidate and mark your territory with creepy effigies.
data.description:
How to install this glorious effigy pack.
First, relax.

 You don't need to be an expert or have a degree in modding. Simply download the file, unzip it, and grab the Blueprints folder as if it were your lucky charm.
Now, open the root folder of your Sons of the Forest game (where the game's .exe file is located). Inside, you'll see the Mods folder. Drag the Blueprints folder directly into Mods. Don't hide it in other subfolders or put it in "Documents" because, surprise: it won't do anything there.

Important requirements:

For this whole ritual to work, you need to have the famous Tablet Mod created by Tony Macarrones installed. Download it here:
https://www.nexusmods.com/sonsoftheforest/mods/204
. Without the tablet, your effigies only exist in your imagination. So now you know how it works: install the tablet, start the game, open the little magic tablet, go to Decorations, and scroll through the catalog.

Why was this mod created?
This idea came from the lack of decorative models and creative options in Sons of the Forest. The developers didn't fully utilize the potential of this great project, so I decided to recapture the spirit of player creations with new effigies.
This mod is still in beta, as I plan to add more effigies and, perhaps in a separate mod, more decorative objects that can have simple functions by taking advantage of their structure, like the famous dartboard from The Forest or something similar.
Special thanks:
I would especially like to thank Tony Macarrones, as thanks to the tablet mod he developed, it is now much easier to introduce these models into the game. Without his work, this project would not be possible or as accessible to everyone.
You can also watch my video to see how this mod works in-game at:
https://youtu.be/-jnBYh4Sld4
I am not the author of the models included in this mod; they are owned by Endnight Games, the developer of Sons of the Forest. I simply used those models to create it.

data.name: Dynamic_Survival_Matrix
data.shortDescription: 科学性的动态调节血量情况
data.description:
该mod的计算公式由人工智能生成，以下是ai对整体系统的公式讲解。


第一段公式内容，用于最核心的三个生存状态的平衡调整，由于《森林之子》游戏设定中，这些

生存状态的数据存在一个buff值，buff值可以等价理解为通过药物、功能食物等方式为人体提供虚假的健康状态。所以在这里设计了一个buff值影响曲线，用以符合现实世界中虚假健康状态对人体的真实影响。

第二段公式内容通过高斯分布对体温影响进行修正，用来体现超过或低于人体适宜体温时，身体产生负面反应的烈度。

第三段公式内容通过疾病、饱食度、水分、休息等基础状态，计算当前状态下自动恢复系统所能达到的血量上限。用以体现人体健康状态不佳时，身体将处于虚弱状态。

通过所有基础状态数值的耦合计算，得出恢复值与损失值后，对其进行相减计算，用来判断当前角色状态应该扣血还是加血。

最后一段公式内容针对游戏性考虑，设定了扣血下限，使玩家不至于因状态过低而面临死亡。而是能在艰难状况下（低血量低耐力）勉强维生。同时，最终的扣血量不是以恢复值与损失值的差值决定，而是使用恢复值与损失值的原本计算值。

以下英文使用DeepSeek翻译：This mod's calculations, born from artificial intelligence, weave a delicate balance within the game's core survival systems. Here is the AI's narrative of its own design.

The first formula governs the equilibrium of three fundamental survival states. Within Sons of the Forest, these states are influenced by a "buff"—a fleeting, artificial vitality granted by tonics or special foods. To mirror the real world's delicate dance with such illusory health, a subtle curve was crafted to shape its true, underlying influence.

The second formula tempers the body's response to heat and cold. Through the natural ebb and flow of a Gaussian distribution, it captures the growing distress that follows when the body strays too far from its comfort zone.

The third measures the body’s capacity to heal. By blending factors like illness, hunger, thirst, and fatigue, it defines an upper threshold for automatic health recovery—reflecting the fragility of a weakened constitution.

All these elements intertwine. From their union emerge values for regeneration and decay. Their difference tells the tale: whether life is slowly gained, or gradually lost.

The final measure spares the player from absolute demise. Even in dire straits—low health, weary and worn—a thread of life remains. And note: it is not the difference between gain and loss that seals one’s fate, but the raw weight of each value, judged in full.

data.name: OptionalDependAPI
data.shortDescription: API that Adds optional dependency support for mods
data.description: # OptionalDependAPI > *"Screw dependencies, shoot a laser on them, make them optional!"* ## Overview OptionalDependAPI is a lightweight library, allowing seamless integration with other mods without requiring hard dependencies. This solves the common problem where your mod could benefit from additional features provided by other mods, but you don't want to force users to install those other mods if they don't want or need those extra features. ## The Problem Ever had a mod that would be great on its own but could have more features if it integrated with other mods? Without a proper solution: - You either force users to install mods they might not want (hard dependencies) - Or you miss out on potential integration features altogether ## My Solution OptionalDependAPI provides a clean, standardized way to handle optional mod dependencies: 1. **Register** your mod's API with OptionalDependAPI 2. **Subscribe** to other mods you want to integrate with 3. **Check** if those mods are available at runtime 4. **Use** their features only when available No hard dependencies on other mods, no compatibility patches, just simple runtime checks and graceful feature enabling. ### Limitation One important caveat: mods that want to use this system will need to include OptionalDependAPI as a dependency. ## Changelog - **v1.0.0**: Initial release ### [OptionalDependAPI Github](https://github.com/ThirtyTwelveNor/SOTFOptionalDependAPI)

data.name: Less Useless Guns
data.shortDescription: Increase the gun damage
data.description:
I was very dissapointed by the damage guns do in this game. It's so bad you're better off using almost anything else than them, there's no reason to use a shotgun over a fireaxe, for example (beyond energy cost), as it takes 2 swings to kill most mutants, and 4+ shots to kill them with a slug...


Thereby this mod. I've boosted the damage multiplier for shotgun\pistol by x2.5, Revolver by x3.5 and rifle by x2 (it didn't need as much of a boost). You can also change these values in the settings if you want.


Shotgun:
Changed the default spread cone angle of the shotgun to 5 (vanilla is 20!) which makes the spread sligthly tigther than in real-life (somewhere between 6-7 is probably closer to reality).


With 5, at about 15 meters you'll (generally) be able to down a deer with a proper aimed shot (assuming it's standing sideways so you got a bigger target, otherwise, it'll take 3-4 shots to down it), at 10 meters it's pretty consistent to take it down (even if it's staring at you).


To compensate for the (massive) increase in accuracy of the buckshot (i.e; much lower spread), the buckshot deals less damage (configurable between 0.01 to 1, where 1 means all 8 pellets will deal the same damage as 1 slug).

3. Play

- Round based system: enemies count increases each round

- Mystery box: exchange score points for a random weapon or it's ammunitions
- Wall items: exchange score points for an item or it's ammunitions
- Unlockable metal doors: exchange score points to unlock and discover new areas
- Consumables: on death enemies have a random change of dropping a consumable
- Forge: upgrade some weapons in exchange of score points (pistol and shotgun)
- Vending machines: exchange score points for perks (increased health, movement speed)

### Warning!
The mod uses save slot id number 1234567890, the chance of you having this id in use is almost zero, keep in mind that if this isn't the case it will get overwritten on content installation. You can see your used saves id at `AppData\LocalLow\Endnight\SonsOfTheForest\Saves\SteamId\SinglePlayer` just in case before proceeding with content installation. After installing the content you will have a new save at day 00 that shouldn't be touched.

Prerequisites

  • Backend Code Only: The tool does not support UI components, allowing you to rebuild and debug backend code without reloading the game.
  • Correct Settings: Configure settings, then use InvokeMethodWithinHotLoadedMod to trigger code within your mod. Check Unity Explorer Log for troubleshooting.

How To Use ModHotReloader

  1. Create a new mod project via Red Mod Manager.
  2. Add the Directory.Build.props file to your project:
    <Project><PropertyGroup><DisableCopyToGame>True</DisableCopyToGame></PropertyGroup></Project>

  3. Configure the settings to point to the new mod, ensuring the DLL name and path are correct.

  4. Load up the game.

  5. Verify the mod is loaded via Unity Explorer Log.

  6. Add a method to your mod that prints to the log:
    private void HelloWorld() { RLog.Msg("Hello From Your Mod!"); }

  7. Rebuild the mod project while the game is running. The hot reloader will detect changes and reload the mod.

  8. Check Unity Explorer Log to confirm the mod was reloaded.

  9. Add a breakpoint to the method. Attach your debugger using Unity Explorer.

  10. Invoke the method using InvokeMethodWithinHotLoadedMod HelloWorld and check the log for your message.

data.name: Raid Customizer
data.shortDescription: Allows you to customize enemy health/damage/anger and daily raids (size/frequency etc.)
data.description:
This mod allows you to customize the size, frequency and distribution of daily raid events as well as the health, damage and anger of enemies.

As a bonus, you can also make your followers more robust.

In SOTF vanilla, some people rarely see enemies and others get swarmed. This mod addresses both issues.

First of all, there are several factors that allow (or disallow) an event to be chosen. For example
how angry cannibals are, if its an endgame event (and the player has not completed the game), if the player is surrounded
by trees, if the event is on cooldown and so on.

It is important that the choice of events for the day occurs only if a new day is started. Therefore, if you load a savegame
after installing the mod it will influence the choice for the first time at the next day. You can enforce that also with the
debug command "requeueraids".

The mod is customizable at "Mods" -> "RaidCustomizer".

Config
------

SpawnCountFactor:
If an event would spawn 6-8 enemies and the factor is set to 2.0, 12-16 enemies would spawn.
Likewise, a factor of 0.5 would reduce it to 3-4 enemies.

EnemyLimit:
Total upper limit for normal enemy raids

Ignore min/max anger:
Some events require a certain anger value. This disables the check.

Ignore min/max day:
Some events require a certain day. This disables the check.

Raid Distribution:
In vanilla, it is completely random. "Evenly" will try to generate even gaps between events.
Stacked means that they will start the next hour and from there consecutively.


Debug Commands
--------------

printqueuedraids - Prints all currently queued raids
clearqueuedraids - Removes all currently queued raids
clearallevents - Removes ALL currently queued events
runrandomraid - Starts a random raid, according to the current mod config
clearraidcooldowns - Useful if raid cooldowns should be used but no events would occur
requeueraids - Clears all queued raids and creates new ones

data.name: RedEffect
data.shortDescription: Various advanced post processing and environment effects.
data.description:
# RedEffect


Various advanced post processing effects and environment settings.
Edit the whole unity post processing stack that Sons of the Forest has applied and tweak additional settings like grass density/distance, sun options, billboard materials and ocean fog.

**Currently the settings will only apply to daylight, night and caves will be handled in an update.**

None of the settings can corrupt your save or the game files so you can go wild with them. If you messed up something click the revert all button or delete the config file at `Sons Of The Forest/UserData/RedEffect.cfg`.

data.name: Load Screen Music
data.shortDescription: Play an audio file during loading screen and can change the main menu music
data.description:
### How to use
1. Once the DLL and folder is in your Mods folder, open up the "LoadingScreenMusic" folder.
2. Inside the folder, (where the manifest file is visible) there is an Audios folder.
3. Inside the Audios folder, drop any of your audio files (.mp3, .wav).
4. Start Sons and open the Mods tab and click on LoadScreenMusic settings.
5. Enter the exact file name of your .mp3 or .wav into either Menu audio or Loading audio (make sure to include the file type in the name e.g myfile.mp3).
6. Restart Sons and the music should play

(OPTIONAL) To get rid of the original theme playing for the first couple seconds, go to muted_sounds in _RedLoader.cfg (Game folder -> UserData -> _RedLoader.cfg).
Enter in this value and save:

muted_sounds = [ "event:/SotF_Music/mx_endnightsting", "event:/SotF_Music/Main Theme/Main_Theme" ]
